q: Arrangement modes are split into two families. Which split is correct?
choices: Temporal (one at a time) vs spatial (many at once)
explain: Temporal = animated/narrative (one scene shown), spatial = comparative (several at once).

q: Which mode belongs to the spatial family?
explain: Comparative shows several scenes at once; LOD is planned but not built.

q: How many arrangement modes are defined in the schema (built or not)?
explain: animated, narrative, comparative, and LOD (LOD unimplemented).

q: What field selects the arrangement mode?
explain: It lives in the sequence block of specs.json.

q: What do all multi-scene arrangements share before they diverge?
explain: Everything runs the shared trunk up to useViewerState, which then forks.

q: Which statement about LOD is true?
choices: It is defined in the schema but not implemented
explain: LOD is a valid schema value with no frontend implementation.

q: Which is NOT a temporal mode?
explain: Comparative is spatial; animated and narrative are temporal.

q: A single-scene dataset is loaded. What does SceneNav render?
explain: With totalScenes <= 1 there is nothing to navigate, so it returns null.

q: What does specs.json contribute to arrangement?
explain: datareps holds geometry; specs adds arrangement mode and its parameters.

q: Where does the actual arrangement logic run?
choices: In the frontend, driven by specs
explain: The pipeline just produces scenes; the frontend interprets the arrangement.

q: Which component is THE fork between arrangement paths?
explain: useViewerState derives isComparative and selects the path.

q: How does useViewerState decide if comparative runs?
explain: A single derived boolean off the arrangement field.

q: Why concentrate the mode decision in one hook?
choices: So every component sees one consistent interpretation of the spec
explain: Single source of derived state; no scattered mode checks.

q: If arrangement is missing from specs entirely, what happens?
choices: isComparative is false; it falls back to default single-scene nav
explain: No arrangement => not comparative; the default manual nav path runs.

q: The fork lives between which two trunk steps?
explain: After load/parse, useViewerState branches into the mode logic.

q: Which hook does useViewerState NOT compose?
explain: useColor is used by shape components, not composed by useViewerState.

q: What drives scene changes in animated mode?
explain: A timer advances the scene automatically.

q: On load, when does useScenePlayback start playing?
explain: isPlaying is initialised from whether the mode is animated.

q: What does the modulo in scene = (prev + 1) % n produce?
choices: It stops at the last scene
explain: % n wraps the index, so animated playback loops.

q: Animated advances with setCurrentScene(prev => ...). Why the functional form?
choices: To read the latest index instead of a stale captured value
explain: The interval callback is created once; the functional update avoids a stale closure.

q: Default auto-play interval when none is given?
explain: interval ?? 1.5 seconds.

q: Animated is best described as which kind of animation?
explain: Each tick swaps the entire scene; nothing is interpolated.

q: Why does only animated show a play/pause button?
choices: togglePlay is only defined for animated; SceneNav shows the button when the callback exists
explain: The presence of togglePlay is the signal to render the control.

q: In animated mode with a domain, what does the counter show?
explain: With a domain present, domainLabelForScene maps the index to its value.

q: In animated mode WITHOUT a domain, what does the counter show?
explain: No domain => fall back to the bare index readout.

q: Pausing animated playback is handled by...
explain: togglePlay toggles the boolean that gates the interval effect.

q: Which is TRUE of animated mode?
choices: It auto-plays on a loop and is machine-paced
It shows several scenes side by side
It uses the inverse value->index map
explain: Animated is the looping, timer-driven temporal mode.

q: If isPlaying is true but only one scene exists, the timer effect...
choices: Does not advance (guarded on scene count)
Loops on the same scene rapidly
explain: The effect bails out when there are not enough scenes.

q: Animated and narrative differ mainly in...
explain: Same engine, different driver.

q: Stopping at the last scene instead of looping would require changing...
choices: The modulo wrap in the advance step
explain: The % n is exactly what makes it loop.

q: The auto-play timer is created using...
explain: A setInterval in a React effect, cleaned up on unmount.

q: What makes the animated effect re-run when you pause/resume?
choices: isPlaying being in its dependency list
explain: Toggling isPlaying re-runs the effect, starting or clearing the timer.

q: Narrative mode is paced by...
explain: Narrative is viewer-driven; you step through it.

q: Narrative step buttons come from which field?
explain: The labels array provides the clickable captions.

q: Clicking a narrative label calls onSceneChange with...
choices: The array index of that label
explain: Labels are positional: labels[i] jumps to scene i.

q: Why does narrative NOT need the value->index map?
choices: The label's array position already IS the scene index
explain: Positional mapping means no numeric conversion is required.

q: When narrative labels are present, the numeric counter is...
choices: Hidden (the labels already name each step)
explain: SceneNav suppresses the counter when labels exist.

q: A narrative sample has a domain but NO labels. What shows?
choices: The numeric year counter via the forward map
explain: No labels => the counter path runs, showing the domain value.

q: Narrative reuses which rendering path?
choices: The same single-scene path as animated
explain: It is single-scene rendering, just viewer-paced.

q: Which is TRUE about narrative vs animated UI?
choices: Narrative shows labels; animated shows play/pause + counter
explain: The control set differs with the mode.

q: If you see years on the buttons in narrative, those years are...
choices: Literal strings in the labels array
explain: Labels can be any text, including year strings; they are not computed.

q: Narrative lets you jump to any step because...
choices: Each label button carries its captured scene index
explain: Direct index jump, no sequential stepping required.

q: Which mode is viewer-paced AND single-scene?
explain: Narrative: one scene at a time, advanced by the user.

q: Narrative with labels [Pre, Boom, Post] has how many scenes shown at once?
explain: Temporal: one scene at a time, even though there are three labels.

q: The narrative counter being hidden is decided by...
choices: Whether a labels array is present (hasLabels)
explain: SceneNav gates the counter on hasLabels, not the mode name.

q: Narrative and animated are implemented as...
explain: Shared hook; the boolean and labels differ.

q: A label click in narrative that is out of range would...
choices: Be impossible (indices come from the array)
explain: Indices are generated from the labels array, so they are always valid.

q: To convert narrative into self-advancing playback you would...
choices: Set arrangement to animated (enabling the timer)
explain: The mode boolean flips the timer on.

q: A comparative config refers to scenes by their...
explain: Selection is expressed in domain values.

q: The renderer, by contrast, addresses scenes by their...
choices: Integer index into the scenes array
explain: Hence the need for a value<->index map.

q: The value->index conversion is the...
explain: Inverse: value in, index out.

q: The index->value conversion (domainLabelForScene) is the...
explain: Forward: index in, value out.

q: Inverse map formula i = round((v - min)/(max - min) * (n - 1)). The round() is there to...
choices: Snap an in-between value to the nearest existing scene
explain: Requested values between scenes resolve to the nearest real one.

q: Domain [2000, 2024], 25 scenes. The index for value 2012 is...
Domain [2000, 2024], 25 scenes. The index for value 2000 is...
explain: round(0) = 0, the first scene.

q: Domain [2000, 2024], 25 scenes. The index for value 2024 is...
Domain [2000, 2024], 25 scenes. The index for value 2006 is...
Domain [0, 10], 11 scenes. The index for value 5 is...
Domain [2000, 2024], 13 scenes (every 2 years). The index for 2012 is...
Forward map, domain [2000,2024], 25 scenes: index 6 gives value...
Forward map, domain [2000,2024], 25 scenes: index 12 gives value...
Why must forward and inverse maps be exact inverses?
choices: So a button labelled 2006 actually selects the 2006 scene
explain: If they disagree, the label misrepresents the chosen scene.

q: The picker labels its buttons using which direction?
explain: It turns each index into its display value.

q: The selection resolves a clicked value using which direction?
explain: It converts the requested value to a scene index.

q: domainLabelForScene with totalScenes = 1 avoids division by zero by...
explain: The max() guards the (n-1) denominator.

q: Which components share domainLabelForScene?
choices: SceneNav, the comparative picker, and the floating 3D labels
explain: One helper keeps the displayed value consistent everywhere.

q: A benefit of selecting by value rather than index is...
choices: It survives the data being regenerated at a different resolution
explain: The index is recomputed from n, so the value still resolves.

q: If a requested value lies exactly between two scenes, the inverse map...
choices: Rounds to the nearest of the two
explain: round() picks the closer scene.

q: The map between value and index is...
explain: A single linear relation, used in both directions.

q: Narrative uses which direction of the map (if any)?
choices: Forward only, and only for the counter when no labels exist
explain: The counter readout uses the forward map; selection is positional, not the inverse.

q: Which is TRUE about the inverse map?
choices: It is the same as domainLabelForScene
It is used in narrative selection
explain: Only comparative selection needs value->index.

q: specs has selection [2000, 2006, 2009]. allowedScenes becomes...
choices: the resolved indices (the comparison is locked)
explain: An explicit selection both seeds and locks the set.

q: specs has no valid selection. The selection falls back to...
explain: No selection => default to [0, 1], allowedScenes stays null.

q: With allowedScenes = null, toggling a scene is...
explain: null means every scene can be toggled.

q: The comparative invariant is: a selected scene can be removed only while...
explain: It can never collapse to an empty stage.

q: Selected indices are kept...
choices: Sorted, so scenes appear in domain order
explain: Sorting keeps display order independent of click sequence.

q: The merged comparative data is computed...
choices: Once in a useMemo when inputs change
explain: Single source of derived state; the canvas gets a ready array.

q: Which function builds the comparative DataRep[][]?
explain: It maps each selected index through mergeSceneWithStage.

q: Each merged comparative scene contains...
choices: Its data points plus the persistent stage
explain: Stage scaffolding is carried into every scene.

q: Always being able to ADD a scene but only REMOVE while >1 remains prevents...
explain: Guarantees at least one scene is always shown.

q: When specs lock the set, arbitrary scenes...
choices: Cannot be added (toggles restricted to allowedScenes)
explain: allowedScenes restricts toggling to the configured subset.

q: The canvas in comparative receives...
explain: It never touches raw data; it gets the derived array.

q: Why precompute the merge in a useMemo rather than in render?
choices: So it only runs when inputs change and every consumer sees the same result
explain: Derived-state-once principle.

q: If the picker is 'locked', that corresponds to allowedScenes being...
explain: A concrete set means the comparison is fixed.

q: Removing the last-but-one selected scene is...
choices: Blocked once only one would remain
explain: You can drop to one, never to zero.

q: Comparative selection state is recomputed when...
explain: It is derived from the data and the spec.

q: Default comparative column count for n scenes is...
explain: Near-square grid unless columns is set in specs.

q: 5 selected scenes, no columns set. Number of columns is...
explain: ceil(sqrt(5)) = 3.

q: 5 scenes, 3 columns. Number of rows is...
9 selected scenes, no columns set. Columns is...
explain: ceil(sqrt(9)) = 3.

q: 4 scenes, no columns set. The grid is...
explain: ceil(sqrt(4)) = 2 cols, ceil(4/2) = 2 rows.

q: Scene at flat index i, with cols columns, sits at column...
explain: col = i mod cols, row = floor(i / cols).

q: Scene at flat index i sits at row...
explain: row = floor(i / cols).

q: A scene's x position is col*gap.x - totalWidth/2. The subtraction...
choices: centers the grid on the origin
explain: Shifting by half the span centers the whole grid.

q: Which gap component spaces the COLUMNS?
explain: x spaces columns, z spaces rows.

q: Which gap component spaces the ROWS (depth)?
explain: z drives row separation.

q: What is gap.y used for in current comparative layouts?
choices: Nothing yet (0); reserved for LOD stacking
explain: Vertical offset is reserved for LOD and is zero now.

q: Each comparative cell gets a year label via...
explain: An HTML label floats above each cell, readable from any angle.

q: The grid stays centered as scenes are added/removed because...
choices: Centering is recomputed over the whole grid each time
It is fixed at the origin regardless
explain: Total width/depth is recomputed, keeping framing symmetric.

q: Overriding the grid shape is done with...
explain: columns sets the column count; rows follow.

q: Comparative reuses which canvas?
explain: Same canvas; ComparativeContent lays scenes out inside it.

q: The big payoff of the grid math is...
choices: Any scene count becomes a centered, readable grid with no per-sample tuning
explain: It generalises to any number of scenes automatically.

q: LOD is intended to swap detail based on...
choices: The viewer's physical proximity to the data stage (AR)
explain: Closer viewer => richer scene, meaningful in AR.

q: Why is LOD hard to trigger in a browser?
choices: There is no natural proximity signal like in AR
explain: A browser lacks the physical-approach trigger; orbit distance could substitute but is not wired up.

q: In the schema, LOD is...
explain: It is defined as a valid mode; only the implementation is missing.

q: Which reserved field hints at the unbuilt LOD feature?
explain: The gap vector's y component is reserved for LOD.

q: Choosing LOD in the current viewer results in...
choices: The path stopping at the fork (not implemented)
explain: No implementation; nothing mode-specific runs.
